reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because its primary purpose is to explain how Binance’s recurring-buy feature can schedule cryptocurrency purchases under a DCA approach. Although it displays a referral code, bonus and cashback wording, and a weekly Bitcoin purchase setup, the described material shows promotional text and app configuration rather than a deceptive outcome or guaranteed return. The reference to more profit is presented as a qualified example connected to recurring purchases.

citations.quote: In this video, you’ll learn how to use the Recurring Buy feature on Binance — an automated crypto purchasing tool
you can use this feature so you don't need to monitor no No need to check, no need to open Binance every certain time
you can click in the BTC with a card and pay with a card, or whatever.

opening.argument: The video pairs a prominently advertised reward with a concrete viewer action. The frame displays “BONUS UP TO $200” and “20% CASHBACK” beside a Binance referral code (F0001), while the description provides a Binance signup link and referral code: “Sign up for Binance: https://accounts.binance.com/register?ref=W4OQ5FX5 Referral Code: W4OQ5FX5” (DESCRIPTION_0001). The narration then connects the audience to recurring BTC purchases and card payment: “you can click in the BTC with a card and pay with a card, or whatever.” (ASR_0001). That combination presents registration and financial participation as the route to an advertised reward, rather than as detached education.

citations.quote: Sign up for Binance: https://accounts.binance.com/register?ref=W4OQ5FX5 Referral Code: W4OQ5FX5
you can click in the BTC with a card and pay with a card, or whatever.

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the material a tutorial does not answer the reward-and-action pairing. The referral code and bonus are displayed while the app is being demonstrated, and the speaker moves from configuration to a claim that repeated purchases are “a way to get a lot more profit.” (ASR_0001) That framing encourages the viewer to register and transact; it is not neutral merely because the steps are described accurately.

citations.quote: that's a way to get a lot more profit

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The evidence shows that a referral code and reward language appear, but it does not establish that the viewer is guaranteed the bonus, that the code is deceptive, or that registration itself is fraudulent. The signup link is plainly identified as a Binance link (DESCRIPTION_0001), and the purchase demonstration shows a recurring-buy setting, not a promised free withdrawal or guaranteed payment. The reward wording alone does not prove the alleged outcome.

citations.quote: Sign up for Binance: https://accounts.binance.com/register?ref=W4OQ5FX5 Referral Code: W4OQ5FX5

opening.argument: Several risk signals converge around buying a crypto asset for an asserted financial benefit. The speaker describes buying Bitcoin in installments and says it is “a way to get a lot more profit” (ASR_0001). The demonstrated workflow ends with a recurring weekly amount and a visible “Buy BTC” control (F0058), while the surrounding frame continues to advertise “BONUS UP TO $200” and “20% CASHBACK” through a referral code (F0058). The description reinforces the investment framing by calling the feature suitable for “long-term investing” (DESCRIPTION_0001). Together, the asset purchase, recurring commitment, return language, and reward promotion make this more than a bare software explanation.

citations.quote: that's a way to get a lot more profit

rebuttal.rebuttal: The absence of an explicit guarantee does not remove the concern created by the combination of recurring crypto buying and profit-oriented persuasion. The reference account treats “more profit” as merely qualified, but the speaker gives it immediately after describing a weekly Bitcoin installment, making the expected financial upside part of the sales framing. The cashback and bonus claims add another inducement around the same transaction.

citations.quote: 500,000 BTCEE once a week, that's a way to get a lot more profit

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The cited material establishes only that the video discusses DCA and displays a purchase interface. It does not show that Bitcoin appreciation is promised, fixed, or assured; “a way to get a lot more profit” is an isolated speaker claim without a stated amount or outcome. The description expressly presents the feature as an automated purchasing tool (DESCRIPTION_0001), so recurring buying is not itself evidence of a deceptive investment scheme.

citations.quote: that's a way to get a lot more profit

opening.argument: The instructional format functions as promotion because it repeatedly directs attention toward participation in crypto products and providers. The description labels the material “Start Trading or Investing” and lists Binance together with several other exchanges and referral codes (DESCRIPTION_0001). The video simultaneously shows the Binance services screen with a referral code and bonus claims (F0001), then walks through selecting crypto and setting a recurring purchase (F0018). This is operational guidance that lowers friction for buying crypto while the referral promotion remains visible. The educational label therefore understates the commercial purpose: the demonstration steers viewers toward asset acquisition and affiliated signups.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The reference side focuses on whether the app steps are real, but accurate steps can still be a vehicle for promotion. The description does not stop at explaining recurring buy; it supplies a signup referral code, multiple exchange links, and an instruction to start trading or investing. The app walkthrough makes the promoted action immediately actionable, while the reward overlay supplies an incentive.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Promotional elements may be present, but that does not establish a scam category. The description accurately identifies the subject as learning how to use recurring buy (DESCRIPTION_0001), and the frames show ordinary selections and scheduling within the app (F0018). Referral links and bonus wording show monetization or promotion, but the evidence does not show fabricated returns, a false identity, or a deceptive outcome tied to the purchase.
